name: The Amber Loop (Recurring Temporal Anomaly Sightings)
description: Since at least 2196, witnesses across multiple tiers have reported a specific and consistent visual anomaly: a stretch of urban environment — always between forty and eighty meters long, always in motion, always identical in description — in which people, vehicles, and debris appear to be repeating a loop of approximately eleven seconds, moving forward and snapping back with no apparent awareness of the repetition. Witnesses describe an amber-gold color cast over the affected zone and a subsonic vibration felt in the chest. The anomaly has been reported in seventeen distinct GLMZ locations over thirty years, never appearing twice in the same place. No BCI recording has ever successfully captured it — playback shows only ordinary street footage — and the phenomenon is absent from all corporate sensor logs. The Amber Loop has accumulated a dedicated community of trackers who cross-reference sighting reports and attempt to predict the next location.
cultural_impact: The Amber Loop has generated a persistent folk mythology in GLMZ around the nature of digital and physical reality, and the tracker community's cross-tier composition — Shelf residents comparing notes with Tier 4 professionals — has made it one of the few genuinely classless social phenomena in the city.
key_figures: Chorus (ELF analyst who first mapped the location pattern)
locations: Witness sites spanning all tiers, no fixed location
The Tracker Archive (informal meeting space, Tier 2 community center)
Sighting 14 location: Junction of Shelf Block 8 and the Elevated Greenway
story_hooks: A new sighting is predicted with unusual confidence by Chorus — but the predicted location is inside a sealed Tier 5 Spire facility, and someone needs to get eyes inside.
A witness to the most recent Amber Loop event claims the eleven-second loop contained a person who doesn't exist — and has footage that somehow captured what BCI recordings cannot.

A corponation quietly begins acquiring properties at every past sighting location — they know something about the Amber Loop that the tracker community doesn't, and they want the next site before anyone else.
